Art. 25 Recht auf Auskunft (Right of access)
1. Die betroffene Person kann beim Verantwortlichen beantragen, dass ihr mitgeteilt werden:

Now the "what to expect" bullets:

- Identity check: expect it; they may refuse until provided (Art. 25(6)); send a copy, consider masking/watermarking; a registered letter from your home address plus account details often suffices.
- Format: PDF/Excel/CSV or download link; possibly huge; may take weeks.
- Content: you'll get what they hold — purchase history, marketing segments, scores; they may withhold trade secrets (e.g., the exact algorithm behind a score, Art. 4 FADP) but must still tell you that automated decisions are made (Art. 21) — and you can ask for human reconsideration.
- Fees: free in principle; possible only in narrow cases (repeat requests within a short period, or a format requiring disproportionate effort); they must announce it in advance and wait for your consent — don't just pay.
- Partial answers: they may send a summary first and data later, or claim Art. 25(5) exceptions (other people's data, secrets) — you can push back or go to the FDPIC.
- No statutory deadline: unlike GDPR's one month, no fixed deadline; 30 days is the norm the FDPIC treats as "without undue delay".
